targets.text: The X3's home screen shows a clock that ticks over every minute while the device is awake, and stops costing anything once it sleeps
Ticking happens only while awake on Home; no tick logic runs in SleepActivity or after deep sleep

HomeActivity::loop() (HomeActivity.cpp:303, no timer today) checks halClock.getTime() and calls requestUpdate() when the local minute differs from the last drawn minute, so both the classic and cover-grid Home layouts tick
A host or on-device check shows exactly one requestUpdate per minute change and none between changes (no redraw storm from the 50 ms idle loop)
The minute tick only runs when the clock is actually shown (clockShowInHeader on and halClock.isAvailable()), so a hidden clock costs no extra refreshes
With Show on home off or no RTC, Home issues zero timer-driven refreshes
The tick must not keep the device awake: requestUpdate() never touches lastActivityTime (main.cpp:819-824), so auto-sleep at sleepTimeoutMinutes (main.cpp:897-901) still fires on schedule
With the tick running, auto-sleep fires at sleepTimeoutMinutes after the last button press, same as with the clock off
The X3 owner looking at the Home screen between books
The only person reading the X3 Home screen is its owner; no multi-user behavior is needed
Today the Home header clock (Settings > System > Clock > Show on home, off by default per CrossPointSettings.h:264) shows the time of the last redraw and goes stale until a button press
Confirmed on the current X3 build: the header clock does not change without a button press
Show on home defaults ON: CrossPointSettings.h:264 clockShowInHeader initializer becomes 1 for the xteink build
A freshly flashed/settings-wiped device shows the clock on Home without any user action

Home keeps a minute-tick counter and renders every 15th tick with HALF_REFRESH instead of FAST_REFRESH (HomeActivity.cpp:482/559); the counter lives in HomeActivity only and never touches lastActivityTime or preventAutoSleep, so sleep timing is unchanged
Over 30 awake minutes on Home, exactly 2 HALF_REFRESH renders occur (ticks 15 and 30); all other ticks are FAST_REFRESH

When the daily routine's Wi-Fi join gets an SNTP answer (trustedtime::startSync in the routine port's joinWifi, callback onTimeSynced in lib/TrustedTime/TrustedTime.cpp:55-70), the routine writes the synced UTC time to the RTC from its own task before Wi-Fi turns off, never from the lwIP callback (which would race the render task's I2C RTC reads via HalClock)
The RTC write happens off the lwIP task and only after SNTP reports completed; with no internet the RTC is left untouched

While the X3 sits awake on Home, the header shows the correct local time, changing within ~10 s of each minute boundary, with a ghost-clearing half refresh every 15 minutes, and it still auto-sleeps on its normal timeout
Verified on the X3 itself, not only in host tests
The X3 doubles as a glanceable bedside/desk clock without a separate device, and the time stays right because the daily sync keeps the RTC honest
The clock is accurate enough to be relied on (within 10 s display lag, RTC within 2 s after a sync)

On the X3, Home left awake for 16 min shows 16 consecutive minute changes, each within 10 s of a reference clock, exactly 1 half refresh (at tick 15), and the device enters sleep at sleepTimeoutMinutes +/- 10 s after the last button press
Measured on the X3 with a reference clock, results recorded in docs/evidence/
After a daily sync with internet reachable, the RTC differs from NTP time by < 2 s (checked via Clock settings row or the [DAILY] serial log)
Measured after a real morning daily sync, recorded in docs/evidence/

HalClock's poll-and-cache (HalClock.cpp:37-54: _cachedUtc, _lastPollMs, _hasCachedTime, no lock) is guarded so the main-loop minute tick and the render task's formatTime can both call it without a torn 64-bit cache read or interleaved RTC I2C transactions
No HalClock member is read or written outside the guard; a host test or code review shows both callers go through it

The daily routine's RTC write uses a new TZ-free HalClock setter (write UTC to the RTC + refresh the cache), never HalClock::syncFromNTP, which rewrites the process TZ via configTzTime (HalClock.cpp:88-93) — the exact TZ churn DailyRoutine.cpp:26-29 forbids because it races the render task
grep shows the routine never calls syncFromNTP/configTzTime/setenv(TZ) on the RTC-write path

The xteink default-ON for Show on home is behind an xteink build flag set in the xteink envs (platformio.ini env:default / env:xteink_release), not a bare change to the shared CrossPointSettings.h:264 initializer, which every board env (x4pro, papermono, eego_a4, ...) also compiles
A non-xteink env build (e.g. x4pro) still defaults clockShowInHeader to 0

The minute-tick and refresh-mode decision (minute changed? which tick is the 15th?) is a pure function covered by the fork's host tests (test/, as SntpPolicy.h is), and each tick logs one line with the minute and FAST/HALF so the 16-minute on-device check (c20) can be read from a serial log
Host tests cover minute change, no change, the 15th-tick HALF, and counter reset on Home re-entry

tasks.summary: HalClock: guard the poll/cache and add a TZ-free UTC setter
acceptance_criteria: lib/hal/HalClock.{h,cpp} only: a FreeRTOS mutex (or portMUX critical section) guards every read/write of _cachedUtc, _hasCachedTime, _lastPollMs and every _sdkRtc call; localTime/getTime/formatTime/syncFromNTP/setTimezone all take it
new bool HalClock::setUtc(int64_t epoch) writes the RTC via _sdkRtc.set and refreshes the cache under the guard; it calls none of setenv, tzset, configTzTime (grep-verifiable)
pio run -e default builds with no new warnings; clang-format-fix clean
tasks.instruction: Fork repo agentculture/xteink-firmware, branch off feat/issue-1 (c6e8b2cf). Keep syncFromNTP's behavior; just route its cache/RTC writes through the guard. A recursive or non-recursive mutex is fine as long as public methods do not re-enter each other while holding it. No AI trailers in fork commits.

tasks.summary: Pure minute-tick decision function with host tests
acceptance_criteria: new header-only src/xteink/ClockTick.h (no Arduino/HAL includes) exposes a function taking (lastMinute or none, nowMinute, ticksSinceHomeEntered) and returning {redraw, half}: redraw only when the minute changed; half on the 15th, 30th, ... tick; first observation after Home entry draws nothing extra

new test/xteink_clock_tick host test registered in test/CMakeLists.txt covers: unchanged minute, minute change, hour/day wrap (59->0), tick 14 FAST, tick 15 HALF, tick 30 HALF, reset on re-entry; ctest passes
tasks.instruction: Mirror src/network/SntpPolicy.h + test/xteink_sync style. Host test build: cmake -S test -B build/test -G Ninja && cmake --build build/test && ctest --test-dir build/test. This task owns test/CMakeLists.txt.

tasks.summary: xteink build flag: Show on home ON and Asia/Jerusalem clock TZ by default
acceptance_criteria: a build flag (e.g. -DXTEINK_CLOCK_DEFAULTS) is set in the xteink envs of platformio.ini (env:default and env:xteink_release); with it, CrossPointSettings.h clockShowInHeader initializes to 1 and an unset clock time zone resolves to the Jerusalem entry (Timezones.cpp:38); without it both stay as today
pio run -e default and pio run -e x4pro both build; a host or static check shows x4pro keeps clockShowInHeader = 0
a saved settings file value still overrides the default (load path at CrossPointSettings.cpp:122 untouched)
tasks.instruction: Files: platformio.ini, src/CrossPointSettings.h, src/util/Timezones.cpp only. Check whether timezones::activeIndex()/applyToClock treat clockTimezone 255 as UTC; make the flag change that fallback, not the stored value. The daily routine's own Jerusalem fallback (DailyRoutine.cpp routineTimezone) stays as is.

tasks.summary: Home: tick the header clock every minute with a half refresh every 15 ticks
acceptance_criteria: src/activities/home/HomeActivity.{h,cpp} only: loop() calls halClock.getTime only when SETTINGS.clockShowInHeader && halClock.isAvailable(), feeds ClockTick, and calls requestUpdate() exactly when it says redraw; nothing is ticked when the clock is hidden
render() uses HALF_REFRESH when the tick said half, otherwise its existing mode, on both the cover-grid (:482) and classic (:559) paths; tick count resets in onEnter
no write to lastActivityTime and no preventAutoSleep override added (grep); each tick logs one LOG_INF line with HH:MM and FAST/HALF
no tick redraw while recents are loading (recentsLoading guard)
tasks.instruction: Depends on t1 (thread-safe getTime) and t2 (ClockTick.h). Keep the change minimal and inside HomeActivity.

tasks.summary: Daily routine: wait up to 8 s for SNTP, then write the RTC
acceptance_criteria: src/xteink/DailyRoutine.{h,cpp}: Port gains sntpCompleted()/waitSntp(budget) and writeRtc(epoch) (implemented via HalClock::setUtc); before wifiOff the routine, when Wi-Fi was up, waits at most min(kClockSyncBudgetMs, remaining cap) only if SNTP has not completed, then writes the RTC on success
on SNTP timeout or no internet the RTC is untouched and the run's status/outcomes are unchanged; the [DAILY] log line reports rtc_written yes/no
test/xteink_daily host tests (fake Port) cover: already-synced (no wait, RTC written), late sync within budget, timeout (RTC untouched), cap nearly exhausted (wait clipped); ctest passes
the RTC write path calls none of syncFromNTP, configTzTime, setenv, tzset (grep)
tasks.instruction: Do not touch test/CMakeLists.txt (t2 owns it); extend the existing test/xteink_daily target. The write happens on the routine's task, never from TrustedTime's onTimeSynced callback.

tasks.summary: Fork PR, gates, merge, and release the build to the X3 server
acceptance_criteria: fork PR feat(xteink): home clock minute tick into feat/issue-1, conventional-commit title, no AI trailers; clang-format-fix clean (exit status checked), host ctest green, pio run -e default and -e x4pro green, harness-smoke all, Sonar gate checked
after merge, uv run python scripts/firmware-release.py release <forkPR#> --fork-checkout <fork worktree> uploads and offers 1.6.5+xteink.<sha8> to device 3; the PR comment is posted
tasks.instruction: Follow docs/firmware-release.md and the x3-flash-protocol memory. No direct flashing: the X3 gets it via Settings > Check for updates (OTA), like c6e8b2cf did.

tasks.summary: On-device: install via Check for updates, flip Show on home, run the 16-minute Home check
acceptance_criteria: before the install, the user confirms on the current build that the header clock does not change without a button press (c11)
after the install the user turns on Settings > System > Clock > Show on home and picks a time zone if the clock shows UTC

with the user's OK to open serial (it resets the X3), a 16-minute serial log on Home shows 16 tick lines, each within 10 s of a reference clock, exactly one HALF (tick 15), then the device sleeps at sleepTimeoutMinutes +/- 10 s after the last press; recorded in docs/evidence/home-clock-validation.md with SSIDs redacted
tasks.instruction: Read the x3-flash-protocol and network-identifier-hygiene memories first. Kill loggers by PID. Leave the device untouched during the 16 minutes.

tasks.summary: Morning check: RTC within 2 s of NTP after a real daily sync
acceptance_criteria: after the next 06:00 daily sync with internet, the [DAILY] line shows rtc_written yes and the clock differs from an NTP reference by < 2 s; recorded in docs/evidence/home-clock-validation.md
tasks.instruction: Prefer a serial log captured with the user's OK; otherwise compare the Clock settings row against a reference clock by eye and say so in the evidence.

risks.text: h5 says a fresh/settings-wiped device shows the clock without user action; proving it on the user's only X3 would wipe its settings, so t3 proves it by build/host check unless the user offers a device to wipe
15-tick HALF_REFRESH may not be enough against ghosting on the X3 UC8253 fast LUT (frame park v1); t7 will show it, and a change would be a /deviate
the clock/home-minute xteink branch stacks on the unpushed ota/daily-sync branch (itself on open PR #4); its PR base depends on how those land
